questions: Should the function handle columns with NaN or infinite values, and if so, how?
Is the threshold of 0.05 used for any decision (e.g., returning a boolean flag) or only for the test's internal significance level?
Should the function drop non-numeric columns automatically, raise an error, or pass them to shapiro (which would fail)?
What should happen if a column has fewer than 3 or more than 5000 observations (scipy's shapiro limits)?
Should the p-values be rounded or formatted in any specific way (e.g., to a certain decimal precision)?
Is the function expected to modify the input DataFrame in any way (e.g., dropping rows) before testing?
Should the function return the p-values in a specific order (e.g., sorted by column name) or preserve the DataFrame's column order?
If the DataFrame is empty or has zero columns, what should the function return (empty dict, error, etc.)?
